news.title: Chloe Kelly and Ella Toone dropped by England after not hitting ‘expected’ level
news.lede: Chelsea’s Lexi Potter gets first call-up to face Greece. Leah Williamson back after injury for World Cup playoff. Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly have been dropped from England’s squad because of their performance levels by Sarina Wiegman, who has given a first call-up to the 20-year-old ­Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter. Toone and Kelly have played key roles in England’s run of three consecutive major tournament finals but Wiegman made clear on Tuesday, when announcing her selection for the Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, that she wants to see more from them for their clubs.

news.title: Football: Soccer-'The emperor is naked': UEFA's Ceferin takes aim at FIFA boss Infantino
news.lede: COPENHAGEN, Sept 29 (Reuters) - UEFA President ⁠Aleksander Ceferin said 'the emperor is naked' on Tuesday in a blistering attack on FIFA President Gianni ⁠Infantino and his failed plan to sell a stake in the governing body's commercial rights to ‌private investors. Addressing the European Football Clubs General Assembly in Copenhagen, Ceferin invoked Hans Christian Andersen's "The Emperor's New Clothes" as he criticised the language FIFA had used to defend Infantino's shelved FIFA Forward Enterprise project. "Almost 200 years ago, he wrote The Emperor's New Clothes," Ceferin said. An emperor is persuaded that he is wearing magnificent ⁠clothes, clothes which he is told only ⁠the foolish or unfit cannot see.

news.title: Amputee Football Eagles Prepare To Tango Türkiye, Spain, Egypt At 2026 WAFF World Cup In Mexico
news.lede: Nigeria’s team for physically challenged players, Special Eagles will step up their preparations for this year’s WAFF Amputee Football World Cup, following the draw ceremony that placed them in Group B along with Türkiye, Spain and Egypt. READ ALSO: Olowookere Glory: “Amputee Sports in Nigeria Is Not Sustainable or Encouraging” | Sports247 Nigeria. Sports247 reports that the Amputee Eagles’ training sessions are bound to get tougher, now that they know the countries they will face, following the draw in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, where 24 nations that qualified from five continents were divided into six groups of four teams each.
